parsed.explanation: Thin-data, high-risk profile. Article 152 is a contested cross-dressing provision that, if enforced, targets presentation directly; its enforcement against visitors is unsourced. Sodomy law remains on the books, with up to life imprisonment for a third offence, though the 2020 amendment removed execution and lashing. The documented official violence (extrajudicial killings, torture) comes from a 2010 report under a prior regime, so it is dated, and the 2019 survey shows low acceptance of homosexuality, with no trans-specific figure. There is no legal gender recognition, healthcare is constrained, and religious edicts block transition. Organised local support has contracted. Vigilante violence and public anti-gay demonstrations show hostile climate. Weighed against this: no documented visitor-specific targeting, no recorded arrests of trans people, and an open question on enforcement. Structural signals (criminalisation, no recourse, hostile governance) carry the rating into the high-risk band.
